decisions.reason: The explicit stereographic construction is mathematically sound, but its one-based labels conflict with the cited native convention x_k=x(k), k<n. Reindexed the inverse to y_0,...,y_N and renamed the last output coordinate t. Norm algebra, compact-ball continuity at infinity and UCT (including Ext(Z,R)=0 when q=1) prove the unchanged statement; this is a notation repair, not a failed cohomology argument.

The published pullback theorem constructs precisely the charts used here: Proof steps 2.1 and 3.1 define the induced chart (q,e)->(q,v), its inverse, and the smooth atlas. F2 explicitly cites the structure constructed there, rather than an arbitrary structure satisfying only the short existence statement. For the global product chart this is exactly Phi; its inverse and pulled-back frame are smooth in this atlas. Rank zero and empty bases require no choice. No item edit is warranted.

F3 overstates the published normal definition by assigning rank N-m without N>=m. An empty m-manifold embeds into smaller ambient dimension, so this rank can be negative. Added N>=m to F3, consistent with the stable-inverse definition. The Statement and Given already assume n>m, and step 3.1 already increases the ambient dimension to m+1 when needed. The orthogonal quotient, canonical product pullback and rank-(n-m) inverse argument therefore remain sound, including empty M; the conclusion is unchanged.

F1 and F2 omit the exact empty-source exceptions in the formal-immersion and normal-quotient definitions: injectivity does not force m<=n on the empty base, and a negative quotient rank is never assigned. Restored the nonempty qualification in F1 and m<=n/rank-zero cases in F2. The lemma itself already assumes n>m, so its quotient has rank n-m even on the empty base under the supplier convention. The metric splitting and canonical Euclidean pullback prove the unchanged stable-inverse claim with AC_omega.

F6 falsely extends positive-dimensional Euclidean embedding Euler vanishing to m=0; a point in R^0 has e=w_0=1. Added m>=1 to that clause and s>=1 to the finite push-off clause. These are used only at m=2s>=2 in steps 2.2-3.1, so all asserted double-point conclusions remain valid. Also corrected the Statement attribution of the tangent-normal identity: the immersion supplier applies for m>0, while m=0 is a direct zero-bundle identity already established in F3. Signed zero counts and regular-homotopy invariance still include rank zero; no rank-zero vanishing is claimed.

The unqualified normal-rank assertion in the Statement and F3 is false for the empty closed m-manifold embedded in R^n with n<m: n-m is negative and cannot be a bundle rank. Added n>=m throughout that assertion. For n>m the cited embedding lemma gives the inverse; the n=m case is retained with the direct proof that di is a fibrewise isomorphism and the normal quotient is zero. Also made k>=1 explicit for the cited immersion tests. The positive-dimension/positive-codimension Euler and top-class clauses already carry their qualifications. Every embedding is an immersion, so all nonimmersion implications and the stronger top-class tests follow unchanged in their valid ranges.

The opening boundary paragraph falsely asserts Euler vanishing for all oriented embedded normal bundles: the point embedded in R^0 has rank-zero Euler class 1. Restored m>=1 and n-m>=1 for Euler vanishing and n>=m for the normal-rank claim, matching the repaired corollary. The RP^3 witness still has positive codimension: its three displayed antipodally equivariant orthonormal fields descend to a tangent frame, so a trivial rank-one inverse has zero Euler and stable w=p=1. Hatcher Example 2.42 gives d_1=0,d_2=2 and H_1=Z/2. Hillman sections 2.1-2.3 establish the locally flat direct-double torsion obstruction by Mayer-Vietoris and duality/UCT, excluding this torsion group. This is a local repair review, not an independent review of my edit.
